# Adjudication Task — Chapter 281

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃281화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|리무진은 일체의 흔들림 없이 도로 위를 질주했다.
  6|
  7|내부에 설치된 냉장고에서 생수를 꺼낸 박지훈은 맞은편에 앉은 장년인에게 권했다.
  8|
  9|“드시겠습니까?”
 10|
 11|“이 상황에? 그리고 남의 물건을 제 것처럼 권하는 버릇은 어디서 배웠지?”
 12|
 13|“그럼 절반만 마시는 건 괜찮겠군요. 지금의 명동 길드가 있기까지 저한테 그 정도 지분은 있으니까요.”
 14|
 15|“…….”
 16|
 17|장년인, 명동 길드장 박태섭은 말없이 생수병을 기울이는 박지훈을 노려봤다.
 18|
 19|“태평하군.”
 20|
 21|딱 절반을 비운 후 푹신한 시트에 몸을 기댄 박지훈이 대답했다.
 22|
 23|“근심해야 할 이유라도 있습니까?”
 24|
 25|“이 사달이 났는데 아무렇지 않다고?”
 26|
 27|“사소한 해프닝일 뿐입니다.”
 28|
 29|“모래탑은 물 한 방울로도 무너지는 법이야.”
 30|
 31|“그건 모래탑이니까요.”
 32|
 33|“명동 길드는 다르다?”
 34|
 35|“소속 헌터 오백 명. 그중 A급 헌터만 스무 명입니다. 이만하면 모래탑이 아니라 철탑이라고 해도 틀린 말이 아닐 텐데요. 그리고…….”
 36|
 37|박지훈의 입꼬리가 부드럽게 올라갔다.
 38|
 39|“명동 길드는 논외로 쳐야죠. ‘그분’이 계시잖습니까.”
 40|
 41|“……그건 사실이지.”
 42|
 43|마지못해 고개를 끄덕이면서도 탐탁지 않은 표정이다. 그런 박태섭의 모습에 박지훈이 물었다.
 44|
 45|“뭡니까? 뭐가 그렇게 불안해서 안절부절못하시는 겁니까?”
 46|
 47|잠시 침묵하던 박태섭이 입을 열었다.
 48|
 49|“느낌.”
 50|
 51|“네?”
 52|
 53|“내 나이쯤 되면 알 수 없는 직감이라는 게 생기거든.”
 54|
 55|하.
 56|
 57|박지훈은 내심 실소를 금치 못했다. 무슨 소리를 하려나 했더니, 결국 환갑 넘은 노인네의 투정이 아닌가.
 58|
 59|‘단순히 느낌이라니. 이 무슨 웃기지도 않는.’
 60|
 61|그런 생각이 얼굴 위로 고스란히 드러났다. 그리고 박태섭은 그 사실을 모를 정도로 연륜이 짧지 않았다.
 62|
 63|“헛소리라고 생각할 수 있겠지. 이해해. 자네 같은 햇병아리들은 알 수 없는 영역이니까.”
 64|
 65|“아, 그렇게 느끼셨다면 죄송합니다.”
 66|
 67|“전혀 진심이 느껴지지 않는 그 말투도 햇병아리라서 할 수 있는 거고.”
 68|
 69|“저로서는 도저히 이해가 안 돼서 말입니다. 뭐가 그렇게 마음에 걸리시는 겁니까?”
 70|
 71|짧은 침묵 끝에 한 사람의 이름이 튀어나왔다.
 72|
 73|“진태경.”
 74|
 75|한숨처럼 내뱉은 이름이다. 11팀과의 연락이 두절된 직후부터 내내 뇌리를 맴돌던 그 이름.
 76|
 77|아주 잠깐, 일이 어그러진 것에 대한 일말의 불안감이라 생각했지만 아니었다.
 78|
 79|대격변마저 버텨 낸 그의 직감이 이 고민의 해답을 내놓았다.
 80|
 81|“놈은 공성포야. 모래탑이 아니라 철탑에도 균열을 만들 수 있는.”
 82|
 83|박태섭은 대답을 기다리지 않고 손을 뻗었다. 박지훈이 남겨둔 생수병을 집어 벌컥벌컥 들이켰다.
 84|
 85|말을 끝마치자 목이 타서 견딜 수 없었다.
 86|
 87|반면, 그 모습을 바라보는 박지훈의 미간은 잔뜩 찌푸려져 있었다.
 88|
 89|‘노인네가 노망이 났나…….’
 90|
 91|일을 처리하는 과정이 조금 매끄럽지 않았음은 인정한다. 특히 블랙 헌터, 11팀에 관해서는 예상치 못한 오류가 있었다.
 92|
 93|하지만 그런 것들을 감안하더라도, 지금 박태섭의 반응은 너무 과했다.
 94|
 95|‘그분’을 절대적으로 신봉하는 박지훈의 심기가 불편해진 것은 당연했다.
 96|
 97|“진태경을 그렇게까지 높게 평가하실 줄은 몰랐는데요.”
 98|
 99|“결과를 보여 줬으니까.”
100|
101|“진태경은 두각을 드러낸 지 얼마 되지 않았습니다.”
102|
103|“그 얼마 안 되는 시간 동안 많은 걸 보여 준 것도 사실이야.”
104|
105|“보여 줬다고요?”
106|
107|박지훈이 비웃음을 머금으며 말을 이었다.
108|
109|“원명훈 그놈은 쓰레기였습니다. 랭커 중에서도 말석. 그것도 한류 열풍이니 뭐니 할 때 적선하듯이 한 번 이름 올려 준 게 전붑니다. 길드장님도 아시잖습니까.”
110|
111|“멍청하고, 탐욕스러운 것으로도 모자라 실력도 유명세로 포장한 놈이었다는 이야기는 들었지.”
112|
113|“그리고 네임드 몬스터요? 말이 네임드 몬스터지, 그 블랙 드레이크는 근 20년 사이 출몰한 네임드 몬스터 중에 가장 약체였습니다. 사체에서 나온 마정석도 A급 몬스터와 큰 차이가 없었어요.”
114|
115|“그래서, 자넨 그 약한 네임드 몬스터를 혼자 잡을 수 있겠나?”
116|
117|“못 할 것도 없지요.”
118|
119|박지훈의 대답은 막힘없었다.
120|
121|그는 스스로의 실력에 자부심이 있었다.
122|
123|천부적인 재능이 있었기에 ‘그분’의 선택을 받는 영광을 누렸고, 서른도 안 된 젊은 나이에 명동 길드장의 맞은 편에 앉아 눈을 맞추며 대화할 수 있는 것이다.
124|
125|그러나 다음 순간 이어지는 질문에는 멈칫할 수밖에 없었다.
126|
127|“그럼 자네가 진태경과 싸운다면? 그를 상대로도 승리를 확신할 수 있나?”
128|
129|“……물론입니다.”
130|
131|이번 대답은 반 박자 느렸다. 그 사실을 깨닫고 지그시 입술을 깨무는 그를 보며 박태섭이 말했다.
132|
133|“방금 그 망설임이 진태경이 어떤 사람인지 말해 주는 것 같은데.”
134|
135|박지훈이 차갑게 대꾸했다.
136|
137|“잠시 옛날 생각이 났을 뿐입니다.”
138|
139|“아, 친구라고 했던가?”
140|
141|“그 얘기는 하고 싶지 않군요. 제가 말씀드리고 싶은 건, 이번 일이 길드장님께서 생각하시는 것만큼 심각한 일이 아니라는 겁니다.”
142|
143|“11팀은 아직 생사도 파악하지 못했고, 현재 국내 최고의 화제를 모으고 있는 유명 인사가 명동 길드 본사에 쳐들어왔는데 심각한 일이 아니다?”
144|
145|“멍청한 놈입니다. 그러니까 순간의 화를 이기지 못하고 겁도 없이 명동 길드 본사에 침입한 거겠죠.”
146|
147|약 10분 전, 1팀장과 통화를 나누던 박지훈은 갑자기 들려온 진태경의 목소리에 놀랐다.
148|
149|그리고 동시에 안심했다.
150|
151|‘일이 쉽게 풀리겠군.’
152|
153|명동 길드에 소속된 헌터는 오백 명이 넘는다. 그중 절반이 레이드로 빠져나갔다고 해도 어마어마한 숫자가 본사에 상주했다.
154|
155|물론 그중에는 길드 최정예인 1팀도 포함되어 있었다.
156|
157|“진태경은 호랑이 소굴로 들어간 겁니다. 놈을 붙잡아 둔 상태에서 교통 정리하면 끝나는 일이에요.”
158|
159|냄새를 맡은 기자들이 끼어든다고 해도 걱정 없다.
160|
161|그에게는, 아니 ‘그분’에게는 카메라와 마이크를 먹통으로 만들 힘이 있기 때문이다.
162|
163|“오늘 안에 깔끔하게 정리하겠습니다.”
164|
165|박태섭은 부쩍 늙은 얼굴로 중얼거렸다.
166|
167|“심상치 않아. 나이를 먹어서 그런가, 슬슬 힘에 부치는군.”
168|
169|“단지 스쳐 지나가는 바람일 뿐입니다. 대격변이라는 태풍까지 버텨 내신 분이 다리가 후들거리면 곤란하죠.”
170|
171|격려보다는 질책이 담긴 말뜻을 알아차린 박태섭이 입을 다문 그때, 어디선가 단조로운 핸드폰 알림이 울렸다.
172|
173|“제 전화는 아닙니다만.”
174|
175|“내 거야.”
176|
177|“누굽니까?”
178|
179|“내 경호 담당인 김 실장. 11팀이 어떻게 됐는지 알아보라고 시켰지. 이제 막 도착한 모양이군.”
180|
181|“잘됐군요. 우선 11팀에 관한 흔적은 전부 지우라고 하십시오.”
182|
183|“지금 나한테 명령하나?”
184|
185|인상을 찡그린 박태섭이 전화를 받았다.
186|
187|“나일세. 어떻게 됐나? 응? 아, 그래.”
188|
189|미간이 찌푸려졌다가, 펴졌다가. 눈동자가 팽창과 수축을 반복한다.
190|
191|표정이 점점 묘해지던 박태섭이 귀에서 핸드폰을 뗐다.
192|
193|“어떻게 됐습니까?”
194|
195|“받아.”
196|
197|박태섭이 자신의 핸드폰을 그에게 건넸다. 이마 위로 핏줄이 불끈 도드라져 보였다.
198|
199|“네?”
200|
201|“어서!”
202|
203|박지훈은 당혹스러운 얼굴로 핸드폰을 건네받아 귀에 댔다.
204|
205|그러자 고양이 발바닥처럼 부드러운 목소리가 그의 귓가를 파고들었다.
206|
207|- 명동 길드 1팀 박지훈 헌터님?
208|
209|박지훈은 듣는 순간 깨달았다.
210|
211|전화를 건 사람은 오다가다 몇 번인가 마주쳤던 김 실장이 아니었다.
212|
213|목소리는 젊었고, 정중하면서도 쉽게 다가갈 수 없는 기운을 물씬 풍겼다.
214|
215|“본인인데, 누구십니까?”
216|
217|느낌이 좋지 않다.
218|
219|본능적인 불안감이 담긴 박지훈의 물음에 낯선 목소리가 대답했다.
220|
221|- 최민우라고 합니다.
222|
223|“누구요?”
224|
225|- 아, 소속은 평화 길드입니다. 직책은 팀장이고요.
226|
227|“……평화 길드?”
228|
229|- 예.
230|
231|이런 씨발. 박지훈의 입술이 달싹거렸다.
232|
233|몇 마디만으로도 어떻게 된 일인지 파악하기에는 충분했다. 평화 길드가 파놓은 함정에 보기 좋게 걸려든 것이다.
234|
235|핸드폰의 주인인 김 실장이 어떻게 되었는지는 안 봐도 뻔하다. 꽁꽁 묶여 기절해 있거나, 자신의 핸드폰이 쓰이는 것을 원통하게 바라보고 있겠지.
236|
237|‘명동 길드, 이 병신 같은 새끼들.’
238|
239|수화기 너머 들려오는 최 팀장의 목소리는 승자의 그것처럼 느긋했다.
240|
241|- 대화를 나누고 싶어서 전화드렸습니다.
242|
243|“그게, 그러니까.”
244|
245|이를 악문 박지훈의 머리가 팽팽 돌아가던 그때, 가슴으로부터 진동이 전해졌다.
246|
247|지금 손에 들고 있는 박태섭의 핸드폰이 아니다.
248|
249|- 박지훈 헌터님?
250|
251|“잠시만. 잠시만요.”
252|
253|박지훈은 남은 손으로 정장 안주머니에서 자신의 핸드폰을 꺼내어 확인했다.
254|
255|문자 한 통이 와 있었고, 발신인은…….
256|
257|
258|
259|[1팀장]
260|
261|
262|
263|됐구나.
264|
265|박지훈의 입가에 안도의 웃음이 맺혔다. 명동 길드라는 호랑이굴로 들어간 진태경이 드디어 무릎을 꿇은 것이 분명했다.
266|
267|저쪽으로 기울었던 저울추가 이제야 맞춰진 셈이다.
268|
269|그러나.
270|
271|“……어?”
272|
273|문자를 확인한 박지훈의 입가에서 웃음이 사라졌다.
274|
275|6인치의 핸드폰 화면을 가득 채운 것은, 진태경을 사로잡았다는 1팀장의 보고가 아닌 한 장의 이미지 파일이었다.
276|
277|‘이게 무슨.’
278|
279|낯익은 얼굴들이다.
280|
281|핏방울이 튄 얼굴로 활짝 웃고 있는 사진 속 청년. 그리고 마치 약에 중독된 사람처럼 파랗게 질린 안색으로 그에게 붙들려 있는 중년인.
282|
283|‘진태경, 1팀장?’
284|
285|그뿐만이 아니다. 두 사람의 등 뒤로 익숙한 배경이 눈에 들어왔다.
286|
287|‘명동 길드 1팀 박지훈 헌터’라고 적힌 자신의 명패는 그들이 지금 어디 있는지 알려 주는 결정적인 단서였다.
288|
289|그리고 하나 더.
290|
291|‘설마…… 아무도 막지 못했다고? 진태경 저놈 하나를?’
292|
293|믿고 싶지 않은 현실.
294|
295|박지훈의 갈 곳 잃은 눈동자가 흔들리던 그 순간이었다.
296|
297|우웅.
298|
299|진동과 함께 새로운 문자가 도착했다. 내용은 짧았지만, 강렬했다.
300|
301|딱 다섯 글자로 박지훈의 멘탈을 으깨 놓았으니까.
302|
303|
304|
305|〈 1팀장
306|
307|
308|
309|1팀장
310|
311|올 때 메로나
312|
313|
314|
315|“이, 이 씨발……!”
316|

[P17]
“Five hundred Hunters under its banner. Twenty of them A-rank. At this point, it wouldn’t be wrong to call it an iron tower instead of a tower of sand. And…”

[P18]
The corners of Park Jihoon’s mouth curved gently upward.

[P19]
“Myeongdong Guild shouldn’t even be part of the comparison. We have ‘that person,’ after all.”

[P20]
“……That’s true.”

[P21]
Park Tae Seop nodded reluctantly, though his expression remained displeased. Park Jihoon studied him.

[P22]
“What is it? What has you so anxious you can’t sit still?”

[P23]
After a brief silence, Park Tae Seop spoke.

[P24]
“A feeling.”

[P25]
“What?”

[P26]
“When you reach my age, you develop instincts you can’t explain.”

[P27]
*Ha.*

[P28]

[P29]
*Just a feeling? What a load of nonsense.*

[P30]
The thought showed plainly on his face, and Park Tae Seop had lived too long not to notice.

[P31]
“You may think it’s nonsense. I understand. It’s beyond greenhorns like you.”

[P32]
“Ah, I’m sorry if you took it that way.”

[P33]
“And only a greenhorn could apologize in a tone without a shred of sincerity.”

[P34]
“I simply don’t understand. What exactly is bothering you so much?”

[P35]

[P36]

[P37]

[P38]

[P39]

[P40]

*Has the old man gone senile?*

[P50]

[P51]

[P52]

[P53]
“Shown us?”

[P54]

[P55]

[P56]

[P57]

[P58]
“Then could you kill that weak Named Monster by yourself?”

[P59]
“I don’t see why not.”

[P60]
Park Jihoon answered without hesitation.

[P61]
He took pride in his own abilities.

[P62]
His natural talent had earned him the honor of being chosen by “that person.” It was why, despite not yet being thirty, he could sit across from the Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild and look him in the eye.

[P63]
But the next question made him falter.

[P64]
“Then what if you fought Jin Taekyung? Are you certain you could defeat him?”

[P65]
“……Of course.”

[P66]
His answer came half a beat late. Realizing it, Park Jihoon pressed his lips together.

[P67]
Park Tae Seop watched him and said, “That hesitation tells me everything I need to know about Jin Taekyung.”

[P68]

[P69]

[P70]

[P71]

[P72]

[P73]

[P74]

[P75]
And relieved.

[P77]

[P78]

[P79]

[P80]

[P81]

[P82]

[P84]

[P85]

[P92]
“Are you giving me orders now?”

[P93]

[P94]

[P95]

[P96]

[P97]
“What happened?”

[P98]
“Take it.”

[P100]
“What?”

[P101]
“Hurry!”

[P102]
Bewildered, Park Jihoon took the phone and pressed it to his ear.

[P103]
A voice as soft as a cat’s paw slipped into it.

[P104]
—Hunter Park Jihoon of Myeongdong Guild Team 1?

[P105]
Park Jihoon knew the instant he heard it.

[P106]
The caller was not Manager Kim, whom he had encountered in passing several times.

[P107]
The voice was young and polite, yet carried an air that discouraged familiarity.

[P108]
“This is Park Jihoon. Who am I speaking to?”

[P109]
Something felt wrong.

[P110]
The unfamiliar voice answered the unease in his question.

[P111]
—My name is Choi Minwoo.

[P112]
“Who?”

[P113]
—Ah, I’m with the Peace Guild. I’m a Team Leader there.

[P114]
“……The Peace Guild?”

[P115]
—Yes.

[P116]
*Fuck.*

[P117]
Park Jihoon’s lips twitched.

[P118]

[P119]

[P120]
*Myeongdong Guild, you useless fucks.*

[P121]
Team Leader Choi’s voice drifted leisurely through the receiver, as relaxed as a victor’s.

[P122]
—I called because I’d like to have a conversation.

[P123]
“Well, the thing is…”

[P124]
Park Jihoon clenched his teeth, his mind racing.

[P125]
Then he felt a vibration against his chest.

[P126]
It had not come from Park Tae Seop’s phone.

[P127]
—Hunter Park Jihoon?

[P128]
“Wait. Just a moment.”

[P129]

[P130]

[P131]
**[Team 1 Leader]**

[P132]
Relief spread across Park Jihoon’s face. Jin Taekyung, who had entered the tiger’s den that was Myeongdong Guild, had finally been forced to his knees.

[P133]
The scales that had tipped against him were balanced again.

[P134]
But then—

[P135]
“……Huh?”

[P136]
The smile vanished from his lips.

[P137]
Filling the six-inch screen was not a report that the Team 1 Leader had captured Jin Taekyung, but a single photograph.

[P138]
*What the hell is this?*

[P139]
He recognized the faces.

[P140]
A young man grinned broadly at the camera, blood spattered across his face. Beside him, caught firmly in his grasp, was a middle-aged man whose complexion had turned as blue as a drug addict’s.

[P141]
*Jin Taekyung…and the Team 1 Leader?*

[P142]
That wasn’t all.

[P143]
The background was familiar too.

[P144]
The nameplate reading *Hunter Park Jihoon, Myeongdong Guild Team 1* made it unmistakably clear where they were.

[P145]
And there was one more thing.

[P146]
*No way… No one could stop him? Just one man?*

[P147]
A reality he did not want to believe.

[P148]
Park Jihoon’s eyes darted helplessly around as they began to tremble.

[P149]
Bzzz.

[P150]
Another text arrived. Its contents were brief but devastating.

[P151]
Five words were enough to shatter Park Jihoon’s composure.

[P152]
> **Team 1 Leader**
>
> Bring Melona when you come.[^1]

[P153]
“You—You fucking…!”

[P154]
Crack.

[P155]
The phone in Park Jihoon’s hand crumpled like a sheet of paper.

[P156]
Watching him, Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop muttered quietly,

[P157]
“We’re fucked.”

[P158]
* * *

[P159]
> **Team Leader Choi**
>
> We’ve captured the people dispatched by Myeongdong Guild.

[P160]
The text was from Team Leader Choi.

[P161]
A few hours earlier, after burning down the safe house used by the Black Hunters, we had split up.

[P162]
Team Leader Choi and the others would lie in ambush to secure solid evidence, while I had insisted on acting alone.

[P163]
He had argued that we absolutely needed to capture something—or someone—that could serve as evidence.

[P164]
*He was right.*

[P165]
Every Black Hunter, including Im Yeongjun, had been managed so meticulously that their identities had already been laundered clean. There wasn’t even the slightest link connecting them to Myeongdong Guild.

[P166]
Team Leader Choi had identified that problem immediately.

[P167]
*He’s always calm and composed.*

[P168]
Looking back, he had never once lost sight of the right path.

[P169]
Having Butler Kim as both an excellent mage and a wise adviser probably helped, but at this point, Choi had to be a natural.

[P170]
*Now we have solid leverage.*

[P171]
On top of the captured Black Hunters, we had official Myeongdong Guild employees in our hands.

[P172]
That should make an excellent shield.

[P173]
*Or a dagger.*

[P174]
I sent him a message thanking him for his hard work, along with the photograph I’d taken earlier.

[P175]
Maybe it was because it was an AdultPhone,[^2] but even a picture taken with my foot came out great.

[P176]
“Maybe I should replace my phone while I’m at it.”

[P177]
Someone flinched at my mutter. It was the Security Team Hunter I’d hired as my personal cameraman for the day.

[P178]
Of course, I wasn’t paying him.

[P179]
“What’s wrong?”

[P180]
“N-Nothing, sir!”

[P181]
“Make yourself comfortable. Don’t just stand there. Sit on the sofa or something.”

[P182]
“I’m comfortable like this!”

[P183]
“You look pretty uncomfortable to me.”

[P184]
“I’m fiiiine!”

[P185]
Was it my imagination, or was there a sob mixed into his shout?

[P186]
As an ordinary Security Team Hunter, he’d just watched me beat the living shit out of Team 1, the Guild’s elite—people he normally wouldn’t even dare look in the eye.

[P187]
His reaction was understandable.

[P188]
*The ones who came later weren’t much different.*

[P189]
The other Myeongdong Guild Hunters who arrived afterward didn’t dare attack me after seeing the scene before them.

[P190]
Quite a few of them were armed with fierce loyalty to the Guild.

[P191]
Unfortunately, they didn’t have the skills to back it up. Everyone who charged me got beaten to a pulp and carried away.

[P192]
After I put down around fifty of them, no one else tried. Park Jihoon’s office became forbidden territory that no one dared enter.

[P193]
I sank into his chair.

[P194]
*He must be racing here like a madman by now.*

[P195]
Just thinking about him made my heart turn cold.

[P196]
A middle-school classmate I had happened to run into on the street after ten long years.

[P197]
*How much of what I saw was the real Park Jihoon?*

[P198]
*Hurry up and get here. Before I get any angrier.*

[P199]
Crack.

[P200]
The armrest snapped beneath my grip.

[P201]
“H-He’s here!”

[P202]
“Guild Master!”

[P203]
A commotion spread like wildfire beyond the office door.

[P204]
At the same time, I sensed two immense presences approaching without hesitation.

[P205]
*He’s here.*

[P206]
The next instant, the door exploded inward with a thunderous roar.

[P207]
BOOM!

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 281

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃281화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|리무진은 일체의 흔들림 없이 도로 위를 질주했다.
  6|
  7|내부에 설치된 냉장고에서 생수를 꺼낸 박지훈은 맞은편에 앉은 장년인에게 권했다.
  8|
  9|“드시겠습니까?”
 10|
 11|“이 상황에? 그리고 남의 물건을 제 것처럼 권하는 버릇은 어디서 배웠지?”
 12|
 13|“그럼 절반만 마시는 건 괜찮겠군요. 지금의 명동 길드가 있기까지 저한테 그 정도 지분은 있으니까요.”
 14|
 15|“…….”
 16|
 17|장년인, 명동 길드장 박태섭은 말없이 생수병을 기울이는 박지훈을 노려봤다.
 18|
 19|“태평하군.”
 20|
 21|딱 절반을 비운 후 푹신한 시트에 몸을 기댄 박지훈이 대답했다.
 22|
 23|“근심해야 할 이유라도 있습니까?”
 24|
 25|“이 사달이 났는데 아무렇지 않다고?”
 26|
 27|“사소한 해프닝일 뿐입니다.”
 28|
 29|“모래탑은 물 한 방울로도 무너지는 법이야.”
 30|
 31|“그건 모래탑이니까요.”
 32|
 33|“명동 길드는 다르다?”
 34|
 35|“소속 헌터 오백 명. 그중 A급 헌터만 스무 명입니다. 이만하면 모래탑이 아니라 철탑이라고 해도 틀린 말이 아닐 텐데요. 그리고…….”
 36|
 37|박지훈의 입꼬리가 부드럽게 올라갔다.
 38|
 39|“명동 길드는 논외로 쳐야죠. ‘그분’이 계시잖습니까.”
 40|
 41|“……그건 사실이지.”
 42|
 43|마지못해 고개를 끄덕이면서도 탐탁지 않은 표정이다. 그런 박태섭의 모습에 박지훈이 물었다.
 44|
 45|“뭡니까? 뭐가 그렇게 불안해서 안절부절못하시는 겁니까?”
 46|
 47|잠시 침묵하던 박태섭이 입을 열었다.
 48|
 49|“느낌.”
 50|
 51|“네?”
 52|
 53|“내 나이쯤 되면 알 수 없는 직감이라는 게 생기거든.”
 54|
 55|하.
 56|
 57|박지훈은 내심 실소를 금치 못했다. 무슨 소리를 하려나 했더니, 결국 환갑 넘은 노인네의 투정이 아닌가.
 58|

“We don’t even know whether Team 11 is alive or dead, and the most talked-about public figure in the country has stormed Myeongdong Guild headquarters. Yet you’re saying this isn’t serious?”

[P73]

[P74]
He had been startled.

[P75]
And relieved.

[P76]
*This will make things easy.*

[P77]

[P78]
Among them was Team 1, the Guild’s elite force.

[P79]
“Jin Taekyung walked straight into the tiger’s den. All we have to do is keep him there while we sort everything out.”

[P80]

[P81]
He had—no, “that person” had—the power to render cameras and microphones useless.

[P82]
“I’ll have everything cleaned up by the end of the day.”

[P83]

[P84]
“It’s only a passing breeze. It wouldn’t do for the legs of a man who survived the Great Cataclysm to start trembling now.”

[P85]
The remark held more reproach than encouragement. Park Tae Seop recognized that and fell silent.

[P86]

[P87]

“Who is it?”

[P94]

[P96]

[P97]
“What happened?”

[P98]
“Take it.”

Park Tae Seop thrust the phone toward him, a vein bulging on his forehead.

[P100]
“What?”

[P101]
“Hurry!”

[P103]
A voice as soft as a cat’s paw slipped into it.

[P104]
—Hunter Park Jihoon of Myeongdong Guild Team 1?

[P105]
Park Jihoon knew the instant he heard it.

[P106]
The caller was not Manager Kim, whom he had encountered in passing several times.

[P107]
The voice was young and polite, yet carried an air that discouraged familiarity.

[P108]
“This is Park Jihoon. Who am I speaking to?”

[P109]
Something felt wrong.

[P110]
The unfamiliar voice answered the unease in his question.

[P111]
—My name is Choi Minwoo.

[P112]
“Who?”

[P113]
—Ah, I’m with the Peace Guild. I’m a Team Leader there.

[P114]
“……The Peace Guild?”

[P115]
—Yes.

[P116]
*Fuck.*

[P117]
Park Jihoon’s lips twitched.

[P118]

[P119]
There was no need to ask what had become of Manager Kim, the phone’s owner. He was either trussed up and unconscious or helplessly watching someone else use his phone.

[P120]
*Myeongdong Guild, you useless fucks.*

[P121]
Team Leader Choi’s voice drifted leisurely through the receiver, as relaxed as a victor’s.

[P122]
—I called because I’d like to have a conversation.

[P123]
“Well, the thing is…”

[P124]
Park Jihoon clenched his teeth, his mind racing.

[P125]

[P126]
It had not come from Park Tae Seop’s phone.

[P127]
—Hunter Park Jihoon?

[P128]
“Wait. Just a moment.”

[P129]

[P130]

[P131]
**[Team 1 Leader]**

[P132]
Relief spread across Park Jihoon’s face. Jin Taekyung, who had entered the tiger’s den that was Myeongdong Guild, had finally been forced to his knees.

[P133]
The scales that had tipped against him were balanced again.

[P134]
But then—

[P135]
“……Huh?”

[P136]
The smile vanished from his lips.

[P137]

[P138]
*What the hell is this?*

He recognized the faces.

[P140]

[P141]
*Jin Taekyung…and the Team 1 Leader?*

[P142]
That wasn’t all.

[P143]
The background was familiar too.

[P144]

[P145]
And there was one more thing.

[P146]
*No way… No one could stop him? Just one man?*

[P147]
A reality he did not want to believe.

[P148]
Park Jihoon’s eyes darted helplessly around as they began to tremble.

[P149]
Bzzz.

[P150]
Another text arrived. Its contents were brief but devastating.

[P151]
Five words were enough to shatter Park Jihoon’s composure.

[P152]

>
> Bring Melona when you come.[^1]

[P153]
“You—You fucking…!”

[P154]
Crack.

[P155]
The phone in Park Jihoon’s hand crumpled like a sheet of paper.

[P156]
Watching him, Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop muttered quietly,

[P157]
“We’re fucked.”

[P158]
* * *

[P159]
> **Team Leader Choi**
>
> We’ve captured the people dispatched by Myeongdong Guild.

[P160]
The text was from Team Leader Choi.

[P161]
A few hours earlier, after burning down the safe house used by the Black Hunters, we had split up.

[P162]
Team Leader Choi and the others would lie in ambush to secure solid evidence, while I had insisted on acting alone.

[P163]
He had argued that we absolutely needed to capture something—or someone—that could serve as evidence.

[P164]
*He was right.*

[P165]
Every Black Hunter, including Im Yeongjun, had been managed so meticulously that their identities had already been laundered clean. There wasn’t even the slightest link connecting them to Myeongdong Guild.

[P166]
Team Leader Choi had identified that problem immediately.

[P167]
*He’s always calm and composed.*

[P168]
Looking back, he had never once lost sight of the right path.

[P169]
Having Butler Kim as both an excellent mage and a wise adviser probably helped, but at this point, Choi had to be a natural.

[P170]
*Now we have solid leverage.*

[P171]
On top of the captured Black Hunters, we had official Myeongdong Guild employees in our hands.

[P172]
That should make an excellent shield.

[P173]
*Or a dagger.*

[P174]
I sent him a message thanking him for his hard work, along with the photograph I’d taken earlier.

[P175]
Maybe it was because it was an AdultPhone,[^2] but even a picture taken with my foot came out great.

[P176]
“Maybe I should replace my phone while I’m at it.”

[P177]
Someone flinched at my mutter. It was the Security Team Hunter I’d hired as my personal cameraman for the day.

[P178]
Of course, I wasn’t paying him.

[P179]
“What’s wrong?”

[P180]
“N-Nothing, sir!”

[P181]
“Make yourself comfortable. Don’t just stand there. Sit on the sofa or something.”

[P182]
“I’m comfortable like this!”

[P183]
“You look pretty uncomfortable to me.”

[P184]
“I’m fiiiine!”

[P185]
Was it my imagination, or was there a sob mixed into his shout?

[P186]
As an ordinary Security Team Hunter, he’d just watched me beat the living shit out of Team 1, the Guild’s elite—people he normally wouldn’t even dare look in the eye.

[P187]
His reaction was understandable.

[P188]
*The ones who came later weren’t much different.*

[P189]
The other Myeongdong Guild Hunters who arrived afterward didn’t dare attack me after seeing the scene before them.

[P190]
Quite a few of them were armed with fierce loyalty to the Guild.

[P191]
Unfortunately, they didn’t have the skills to back it up. Everyone who charged me got beaten to a pulp and carried away.

[P192]
After I put down around fifty of them, no one else tried. Park Jihoon’s office became forbidden territory that no one dared enter.

[P193]
I sank into his chair.

[P194]
*He must be racing here like a madman by now.*

[P195]
Just thinking about him made my heart turn cold.

[P196]
A middle-school classmate I had happened to run into on the street after ten long years.

[P197]
*How much of what I saw was the real Park Jihoon?*

[P198]
*Hurry up and get here. Before I get any angrier.*

[P199]
Crack.

[P200]
The armrest snapped beneath my grip.

[P201]
“H-He’s here!”

[P202]
“Guild Master!”

[P203]
A commotion spread like wildfire beyond the office door.

[P204]
At the same time, I sensed two immense presences approaching without hesitation.

[P205]
*He’s here.*

[P206]
The next instant, the door exploded inward with a thunderous roar.

[P207]
BOOM!

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
